title: Diagonal argument: one subsequence along which countably many families of real sequences all converge
statement: Let ι be a type, (F_m)_{m∈ℕ} a sequence of subsets of ι, and s : ι → ℕ → ℝ. Suppose that for every m ∈ ℕ and every strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ there is a strictly increasing θ : ℕ → ℕ such that for every i ∈ F_m the real sequence (s(i, ψ(θ(j))))_{j∈ℕ} converges. Then there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that for every m ∈ ℕ and every i ∈ F_m the real sequence (s(i, φ(j)))_{j∈ℕ} converges.
lean_statement: ∀ (ι : Type) (F : ℕ → Set ι) (s : ι → ℕ → ℝ), (∀ (m : ℕ) (ψ : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono ψ → ∃ θ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono θ ∧ ∀ i ∈ F m, ∃ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun j => s i (ψ (θ j))) atTop (𝓝 c)) → ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, ∀ i ∈ F m, ∃ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun j => s i (φ j)) atTop (𝓝 c)
